newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher for fourth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher for fourth straight day.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly higher on Tuesday, the fourth consecutive rise, and brokers said they expected a firming trend through the year-end.
The index ended up 3.72 points or 0.05 percent at 6,935.72, off a 6,964.24 high. Turnover was an active T$46 billion.

"Though expecting a firming trend ahead, investors were quite cautious as an expected fourth-quarter economic recovery was not apparent," said Oliver Fang, international sales head at National Securities.
Plastics rose on expected raw material price hikes in early 1997, with Nan Ya up 50 cents to T$65.5.
Steel shares rose on increases in steel rod prices, with Kuei Hung up 70 cents to T$23.1.
Transport, electrics and cement shares also rose, but financials and contructions, the main recent gainers, fell.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend partly because of expected window-dressing by local securities investment trust firms on the last two trading days of 1996: December 30 and 31.

"Several state funds are expected to commssion local securities investment trust firms to manage stock investment for them in 1997, and this should force these trust firms to beautify their accounts in order to be selected," Fang said.
The market will be closed on Wednesday for a Taiwan holiday. Trading resumes on Thursday.
Brokers said they expected stable trade through the week and a possible push through psychological resistance at the 7,000 points for the year's final sessions on December 30 or 31.
"The index likely will consolidate in a narrow 6,900-7,000 range from Thursday to Saturday, and then stand above 7,000 points on the last two days of the year," Fang said.
